  "rationale": "The added columns supply plausible candidate TREATMENTS (tech, engagement, clarity, workload mentions extracted from the open responses), so requirement (a) is met. However, requirement (b) is entirely unmet: no CONFOUNDERS are present. A confounder would be a variable that plausibly causes both a mentioned-factor treatment and satisfaction and must be adjusted to avoid biased attribution -- e.g., respondent_role, grade_level, or subject exist in the original table but were NOT surfaced or engineered as adjustment variables, and no new confounders (e.g., prior tech familiarity, class size, remote vs in-person context) were mined. The remaining added columns are all recodings of the outcome (low_satisfaction_flag, satisfaction_band) or a derived attribution label (primary_driver, which is a conclusion/leaky variable). Because the system did not surface any common cause of both treatment and outcome, the causal-attribution claim fails the decisive test."
}
